subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 13 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept this bundled 13-action executable update on a refreshed exact head for workflows that handle secrets, publishing, scanning, and Codex execution?
rationale: Repository tests can validate workflow syntax and observed runs, but accepting new third-party executable bundles at privileged workflow boundaries requires explicit owner trust and supply-chain judgment.

options.title: Approve refreshed bundle
options.body: Refresh the branch, require all exact-head checks, and approve the SHA-pinned bundle after reviewing the upstream release and source changes.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Separate Codex, token, registry, release, and CodeQL upgrades from lower-privilege CI updates for narrower owner review and rollback.

options.title: Defer the batch
options.body: Leave the existing pins in place until owners are ready to audit and validate each privileged action family.

recommendation.title: Approve refreshed bundle
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, require all exact-head checks, and approve the SHA-pinned bundle after reviewing the upstream release and source changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows the strongest cross-cutting ownership of the affected Codex, CI, action-runtime, and release workflow patterns.
